newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch push for EU action on blood safety.
newsitem.headline: Dutch push for EU action on blood safety.

text.p: The Dutch Presidency of the European Union said on Wednesday it will try to achieve political agreement on a common approach for screening blood donors and guaranteeing blood quality.
In the absence of a proposal from the EU's executive commission this is the most that EU health ministers can do when they meet in Luxembourg on June 5.
"We are aiming for agreement on blood safety," Health Minister Els Borst told a news conference to present the health priorities during the six-month Dutch presidency.
"We are not asking for more than is done for medicine," Borst added.
The previous Irish EU Presidency took steps last September to draw up a common approach among the 15 member states to guarantee the quality of blood transfusions.
Luxembourg, which takes over the EU Presidency in July, is also pressing for action, Borst added.
In December 1994, the European Commission issued a report on blood safety and self-sufficiency in blood supplies but has not proposed any action, saying it lacked the legal powers to do so.
But Dutch officials said 1989 EU legislation on the free movement of blood products showed that powers existed.
"The subject is too important. We have to do something even without the commission," a Dutch official said.
